facts.text: LoDo’s roots trace back to 1858 when gold was found at the confluence of the South Platte River and Cherry Creek, sparking Denver’s founding.
General William Larimer planted the first cottonwood logs in 1858 on a square‑mile plot that would become LoDo, making it Denver’s oldest neighborhood.
The historic B‑7 district in LoDo stretches from Cherry Creek to 20th Street, excluding Union Station, preserving the city’s original street grid.
The 1891 Oxford Hotel, now on the National Register, stands as one of LoDo’s oldest surviving commercial buildings.
Union Station, the city’s original rail hub, greeted travelers with LoDo’s first storefronts, making the neighborhood the first sight for newcomers.
The 1988 Wynkoop Brewing Company, founded by former Governor John Hickenlooper, still hosts the annual “Beerdrinker of the Year” contest in its banquet hall.
